title: The classic three-moduli RNS set {2^n-1, 2^n, 2^n+1} for computer arithmetic

problemStatement.formal: \text{Show that } \{2^n-1,\,2^n,\,2^n+1\} \text{ is a valid pairwise-coprime RNS base with dynamic range } 2^{3n}-2^n \text{ and is balanced.}
problemStatement.plain: The canonical 'most efficient' RNS base in hardware practice is the three-moduli set {2^n-1, 2^n, 2^n+1}. Formalize that it is pairwise coprime (n >= 1), that its dynamic range is exactly 2^(3n) - 2^n, that it is balanced (widest channel < 2x narrowest), and that the partial-product reconstruction step is well-defined.
whyMatters: The set {2^n-1, 2^n, 2^n+1} is the single most-cited efficient RNS base in computer-arithmetic hardware (Soderstrand 1986): three n-bit channels, ~3n-bit dynamic range, with two channels admitting trivial modular reduction.
Provides a concrete, fully constructive characterization complementing the general efficiency criteria of the parent file.

insights: The three-moduli set is self-balancing: all three moduli lie within a factor 2 of each other, so the critical-path (widest) channel is nearly minimal for the dynamic range achieved.
Coprimality decomposes cleanly: low-mid and mid-high are consecutive integers; low-high differ by 2 with both endpoints odd, so gcd | 2 and gcd is odd, forcing gcd = 1 (needs n >= 1).
Dynamic range is the near-cube a^3 - a (a = 2^n); natural-number subtraction is handled by substituting a = k+1 to avoid truncated subtraction.
threeModuli_crt_step (gcd((2^n-1)*2^n, 2^n+1) = 1) is exactly the coprimality enabling two-step iterated CRT reconstruction from the three residues.
